column2: The kitchen smelled of burnt sugar.
Dana set the pan in the sink and ran the tap over it. "That is the second one this week."
Marcus did not look up from his phone. "Third."
The tap hissed against the hot metal and the smell got worse.
He put the phone face down on the counter. "What do you want me to say?"
Something. Anything that is not a number.
Marcus laughed, which was the wrong thing to do, and he knew it before the sound was finished. "Sorry."
Dana turned the tap off. "I am going to bed."
She was at the door before he spoke again, and she stopped without turning around.
I did not mean third like it mattered, said Marcus.
I know what you meant, she said to Marcus, and went upstairs.
He stood in the kitchen for a while after that, listening to the pipes cool.
